meta.source: Coded from the published QP and mark scheme (1MA1_3H_2506). Derived metadata only — question numbers, marks and skill tags. No exam question text transcribed.
meta.note: Marks per part read from the question paper's own part totals and checked against the printed 80. Questions 1 to 8 are the overlap questions shared with 3F (3F q22 to q30) and are tagged identically there.

coding_notes: q7 tagged coordinates alone, matching the same question on 3F. The mark scheme's second step is a proportional step along the segment, but tagging proportion would credit the whole fractions-and-percentages chain beneath it.

q10 tagged exact_calculations + significant_figures: the item is a calculator-entry question whose second demand is the rounding. Neither trig node is tagged — the calculator does the trigonometry and nothing about triangles is tested.

q13 (match four equations to their graph shapes) tagged sketching_functions: recognising the shape of a cubic, a reciprocal, a negative quadratic and an exponential is what that node covers, and the taxonomy has no separate 'recognise graph shapes' skill.

q15 (at least two of three with replacement) tagged combined_events + systematic_listing. combined_events is the multiplication of independent probabilities; systematic_listing is the enumeration of the three orderings, and it is a root skill so it costs nothing extra. tree_diagrams was rejected because it would additionally credit frequency_trees.
q17 tagged algebraic_fractions + solving_linear_equations — combining two algebraic fractions over a common denominator, then solving what is left.
q20 tagged circle_theorem_angle_at_centre + circle_theorem_cyclic_quadrilateral, the two theorems the mark scheme names for the two routes through the question.
q22 tagged equation_of_a_circle + perpendicular_gradients: the tangent point is found from the radius perpendicular to the given line.
